The closest match is “Sympathetic Framing: Evaluating AI Alignment across Sociodemographic Groups,” by Haran Shani-Narkiss, Michael Fire, and Oren Tsur. It studies whether LLM alignment with human emotional judgments varies across sociodemographic subgroups, and finds the leading models are broadly aligned across age, gender, education, prior geopolitical knowledge, and conflict predispositions, with some statistically significant group differences [1].

If you meant broader work on sociodemographic effects in alignment, related papers here look at group-specific sycophancy in demographic alignment [3], persona cues and bias in personalization [6], identity-dependent degradation in response quality [10], and modeling human perspectives with socio-demographic representations [9].
